edges.description: In cultured hEDS/HSD dermal fibroblasts, fibronectin-matrix disassembly and altered integrin recruitment promote the αvβ3–ILK–Snail1 transition pathway. The initiating extracellular ligands and some intracellular intermediates remain unresolved; this model-level relation does not establish a route to clinical joint instability.

nodes.description: Joint pain is a very frequent musculoskeletal manifestation in hEDS.

Cultured hEDS/HSD dermal fibroblasts show collagen/fibronectin matrix disorganization and altered matrix-receptor organization. Excessive matrix remodeling is a candidate cellular mechanism. The upstream etiology and causal contribution of these culture findings to joint instability or other clinical manifestations remain unresolved.

evidence.snippet: Currently, no underlying genetic, epigenetic, or metabolomic etiology has been identified for hEDS.

nodes.description: Chronic pain is common and may be distinct from acute injury pain.

evidence.snippet: Subluxations, dislocations, and soft tissue injury are common; they may occur spontaneously or with minimal trauma and can be acutely painful.

nodes.description: Generalized joint hypermobility is the central diagnostic musculoskeletal feature of hEDS.

evidence.snippet: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (hEDS) is characterized by generalized joint hypermobility, joint instability, pain, soft and hyperextensible skin with atrophic scars and easy bruising, dental crowding, abdominal hernias, pelvic organ prolapse, marfanoid body habitus, mitral valve prolapse, and aortic root dilatation.

nodes.description: Joint instability permits subluxations, dislocations, and recurrent joint or soft-tissue injury. Mechanical injury contributes to acute joint pain and chronic musculoskeletal pain, but does not account for every neuropathic or widespread pain presentation.

Chronic pain, distinct from that associated with acute injury, is common and often neuropathic in nature.

nodes.description: hEDS/HSD patient fibroblasts can acquire a migrating myofibroblast-like phenotype with alpha-smooth muscle actin stress fibers, cadherin-11, MMP9, and inflammatory mediator changes through alpha-v-beta-3 integrin/ILK/Snail1 signaling. This remains model evidence rather than a validated diagnostic biomarker.

evidence.snippet: In hEDS and HSD cells, the αvβ3 integrin was shown to be involved in the fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition by a transduction pathway involving ILK that signals to the transcription factor Snail1

evidence.reference_title: Multifaced Roles of the αvβ3 Integrin in Ehlers-Danlos and Arterial Tortuosity Syndromes' Dermal Fibroblasts.
evidence.snippet: hEDS and HSD cells exhibit a peculiar in vitro myofibroblast-like phenotype characterized by organization of the α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) cytoskeleton, expression of the cadherin-11, and enhanced migratory capability, probably because they synthesize high levels of MMP9, a collagenase also able to digest FN into proteolytic fragments

nodes.description: Sleep disorders, including apnea, can occur as part of the hEDS multisystem phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Chronic fatigue, functional bowel disorders, cardiovascular autonomic dysfunction, swallow and phonation disorders, sleep disorders including apnea, migraine, entrapment and peripheral neuropathies, inflammation from mast cell activation disorders, anxiety disorders, and urogynecologic disorders are common.
